paras: The whipping of Charlie Stark took place on Sunday, August 16, 1903, at Turkey Hill in Abbeville County, South Carolina, when a crowd of armed men seized a young Black man from Georgia accused of prowling at a young woman's window. Members of the crowd called for him to be lynched, but after a vote they flogged him and ordered him away. The local paper headed the story "Barely Escaped Lynching."

The Abbeville Press and Banner said Stark had worked for a Sharon-neighborhood farmer the year before and run away, "slipping his contract." About a week before his capture, it said, he began raising the window sash of a room where a local man's daughter slept, and fled when she gave the alarm. The Bamberg Herald said instead that he called her name in a low voice and that she called her brother.

After a second visit on Saturday night, August 15, a party tracked him on Sunday morning to Turkey Hill. More than fifty armed men gathered; some called to "lynch him," others to burn or drown him, and a fire was kindled. A "jury" then voted three for lynching him and seven against. The Bamberg Herald said older men persuaded the crowd not to kill him and that he received 210 lashes with a buggy trace. He was whipped in the public road and turned loose with orders never to return.

The Press and Banner said Stark admitted being the man sought and claimed he wanted someone to give him peaches, an account from his captors' side only. No report of arrests or prosecution of the whippers appears in the coverage.

Only two South Carolina weeklies carried it; no Black-press account appears. The Abbeville paper printed it on August 19 among the social notes of its "East End" column, praising the "wise counsels of older heads" and remarking that in Georgia his fate "would most likely been very different." The Bamberg Herald's item of August 20, headed "A 'Peeping Tom' Flogged," said he came "evidently for an evil purpose" and reported the lashes without comment.

accounts.label: Abbeville local correspondent ('M', East End column)
accounts.gist: Stark tried the window twice, was tracked by his footprints, captured at Turkey Hill, faced a crowd of 50+ calling for lynching, burning or drowning, and after a 3-7 'jury' vote was whipped and banished; he is said to have confessed and claimed he wanted peaches.

accounts.label: Bamberg Herald item
accounts.gist: Stark called the young woman's name at her window 'evidently for an evil purpose'; on his second visit neighborhood men chased him down near the Island ford, meant to kill him, but older men prevailed and he got 210 lashes with a buggy trace.

accounts.label: Captors' claim of confession
accounts.gist: Stark admitted he was the man sought and said he was trying to rouse someone to give him peaches; reported only from the captors' side.

framing.detail: The Abbeville paper headed it 'Barely Escaped Lynching', praised the 'wise counsels of older heads', said his fate would have been different in Georgia, and closed with sympathy for the 'popular and well beloved' young woman, without criticizing the whipping.
The Bamberg Herald's 'A "Peeping Tom" Flogged' asserted he came 'evidently for an evil purpose' and reported the 210 lashes without comment.
